chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman bin A'yun, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forgave a man from the people of the desert due to two phrases with which he supplicated. He said: "O Allah, if You punish me, then I am deserving of that; and if You forgive me, then You are deserving of that." So Allah forgave him.'

key_terms.أَهْلٌ لِذَلِكَ: Deserving of that / Worthy of it

ai.seo_question: What is the short supplication for forgiveness mentioned in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrates that a man from the Bedouins was forgiven by Allah for a supplication consisting of two phrases acknowledging human unworthiness for punishment and divine worthiness for forgiveness. This highlights the theological concept of divine mercy coupled with human humility. In Shia scholarship, this hadith is often cited to demonstrate the efficacy of *tawadu'* (humility) and the balance between *khawf* (fear) and *raja'* (hope), illustrating that sincere recognition of one's own inadequacy alongside God's absolute capacity to forgive is sufficient for divine acceptance.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Ayn who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic had Forgiven a man from the people of the valleys due to two phrases he supplicated with. He said, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! If You<sup>azwj</sup> were to Punish me, so I am deserving of that, and if You<sup>azwj</sup> were to Forgive me, so You<sup>azwj</sup> are Rightful with it’. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Forgave him’.
en.sarwar: 8. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from ibn Mahbub from Aban from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘A’Yun who has said the following:

“Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, forgave a man from the village by two words with which he pleaded before Allah. He said, O Lord, if You punish me, it is because I deserve it and if You forgive me it is worthy of You (Your greatness) and (for this) Allah granted him forgiveness.’”
